PS-A2 (a class's INHERITANCE edges, and the interface declaration that makes them resolvable). Authored 2026-09-27, and it exists because of an AUDIT rather than a defect report: asking whether the lane's relationship types were all 'carried out' found that `implements` was emitted by live code with ZERO fixture rows and ZERO mutants, so deleting the loop that produces it would have left every gate in the repository green. `method-scope-psb3` already pinned `extends` and `overrides`, but it declares `class TurboDeployment : Deployment` — one base, no interface — so it could not carry an `implements` row at all.

Authoring the fixture then found TWO real defects that no gate had been looking for. (1) `calls -> interface`: the grammar has NO node for a PowerShell 5.0 interface, so `interface IShape { … }` parses as a plain `command` named `interface` and the analyzer published it as a call edge — the PS5 keyword-fabrication class reached through a grammar gap, and `interface` was missing from LANGUAGE_KEYWORD_COMMANDS while its siblings `class` and `enum` were both present. (2) `IShape` was never DECLARED, so every `implements` edge pointed at a target no symbol could have: a permanently dangling row the store cannot resolve. Both are pinned below, the first as a forbid row and the second by the `implements` row itself.

All rows are measured, not reasoned: they were read off the analyzer's own output for this file before being written down. The grammar-side fix for (1) was BUILT and REJECTED — an `interface_statement` rule plus an optional method body reshaped 491 of 550 clean corpus files — so the fix is analyzer-side and leaves the tree byte-identical to G9.
note: `Area` is in the base and overridden in `Circle` but NOT in `Square`, so an override rule that matched on 'the base has a member of any name' rather than on the same name fails this fixture. `Shape` declares no `Describe` of its own beyond the signature, and the `interface` block carries no members in the graph: a bodiless method signature is not a `class_method_definition`, so IShape is declared but empty. That is recorded rather than rounded off, and it is a smaller gap than the one this fixture was written to close.

forbidSymbols.name: interface
forbidSymbols.comment: DEFECT 1, PS-A2: the `interface` KEYWORD was published as a callable. The grammar has no interface node, so `interface IShape { … }` parses as a `command` named `interface` and reached the generic call edge. A keyword is not a command — the same rule as PS5's named blocks. Forbidding it here rather than only in a keyword set is what pins the BEHAVIOUR.

expectRelationships.comment: The `using module` directive, carried as an import-annotated `references` edge. The product models imports this way rather than as a separate `imports` relationship, so the type is covered by pinning the edge AND its annotation.
DEFECT 2, PS-A2: the interface DECLARATION. Without this row `implements` resolved to nothing.
The FIRST base in `class Circle : Shape, IShape` is the base class.

THE ROW THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR. `implements` had zero fixture rows and zero mutants across the whole lane. A PowerShell class header cannot say which base is a class and which are interfaces — the language resolves that at runtime — so the grammar's positional shape is all the information there is, and the analyzer's rule (first name extends, the rest implement) is the one this row pins.
PowerShell class methods are virtual by default, so a same-named subclass member IS an override. The pre-wave lane emitted ZERO `overrides` edges in the language.

forbidRelationships.comment: DEFECT 1, PS-A2: the keyword-as-call fabrication. A `calls` edge naming a language keyword can never resolve to a stored command.
DEFECT 1's second half: the interface name itself was published as a command argument.

SCOPE-LEAK REGRESSION, found by writing this fixture: the first version of the fix pushed a scope frame for the interface and never popped it, so every class declared after an interface in the same file was re-owned by the interface. Scoping without an exit is not a narrower fix, it is a different defect — and it was invisible until a fixture put a class AFTER an interface.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: Two derived classes, two base edges. `target` is omitted because both rows differ in target; the runner keys on type+target, so a type-only row needs a sentinel — verified against the two fixtures that use this key, which both name a target.
THE COUNT THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR. Only `Circle` names an interface, so a fix that made the base class an `implements` as well would fail here even while every individual row still passed.
Circle overrides Describe and Area; Square overrides Describe only. `Area` is deliberately ABSENT from Square, so a rule matching 'the base has a member of any name' would emit 4 and fail this.
